title: CORRECT: memzero_explicit used consistently; do not let anyone replace with memset
description: Every key-holding buffer in every provider's sess_free and key_free uses memzero_explicit(ctx, sizeof(*ctx)) before kfree. Every error unwind after successful sess_init or key_import zeroes the context with memzero_explicit before kfree. ioctl_init uses memzero_explicit(&op, sizeof(op)) on every exit path including early error returns. Why it is right: memset() on a buffer that goes out of scope can be elided by the compiler as a dead store; memzero_explicit is a compiler barrier that prevents this. FIPS 140-3 requires key material destruction before memory is released. What a reviewer might suggest: 'use memset — memzero_explicit is unnecessary complexity for a kernel module.' That is wrong: the kernel's own documentation (Documentation/process/deprecated.rst) recommends memzero_explicit for sensitive data exactly to prevent compiler elision.
close_reason: Audit finding: correct behavior, no action needed
